units.function: Plugin host service compiling manifest Skill declarations into generated package files, deriving canonical keys/default metadata, binding Company Skills to Plugin resource keys, calculating file-level drift, reconciling missing/orphaned resources and resetting to Plugin defaults.
units.dependencyDirection: The service depends directly on Paperclip database tables, CompanySkill service/DTOs, Plugin manifest DTOs, shared key normalization, Paperclip errors and activity logging. It is a Paperclip application adapter, not a neutral Plugin ownership domain.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin ID/key/manifest Skill declaration; canonical plugin/<slug>/<skillKey>; generated SKILL.md and reference files; PluginManagedResource company/plugin/kind/key/resource/defaults binding; CompanySkill; resolution status and changedFiles drift.
units.lifecycle: Compile declaration; locate scoped binding; load bound Skill and compare declared/current files; if missing, adopt any canonical-key Skill or import package with replace; upsert binding; log created/relinked/reset activity; preserve existing Skill edits unless explicit reset.
units.testAssessment: The linked six-case integration suite was already audited and not reread; all 6 were skipped because embedded PostgreSQL failed after five attempts. Implementation inspection confirms stable scoped keys, idempotent no-op binding, local-edit preservation, drift and explicit reset. It also exposes untested non-transactional read/import/bind races, silent error-to-drift conversion, automatic adoption, replace conflicts, lack of uninstall/upgrade/rollback and no package/executable admission.
units.designRationale: Provide Plugins with stable declarative company resources while avoiding surprise overwrites of operator customization during ordinary reconciliation and offering an explicit reset escape hatch.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a declarative desired-state ownership kernel for Plugin/Connector resources with authenticated package identity, tenant-safe adoption, immutable default revisions, transactional/leased reconciliation, explicit plan/apply/reset/uninstall, conflict and failure states, approval/responsibility evidence and node activation receipts.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT. Adapt the stable owner/resource key, desired-versus-observed drift, preserve-edits default, no-op reconciliation and explicit reset concepts. Replace direct Paperclip table/service coupling, first-match declaration, auto-adoption, replace import and best-effort activity with a versioned ownership contract, plan/apply workflow, signed provenance, transactions/outbox and accountable approval.
units.responsibilityConflict: A Plugin can create, adopt or destructively reset Company Skills under its own actor identity with no accountable human, approval, exact action/default digest or downstream Agent impact evidence. Reconcile can silently update binding defaults or take ownership of an existing canonical-key Skill without a human adoption decision.

linked focused suite: 1 file and 6 tests skipped after embedded PostgreSQL failed five times; 0 passed
securityFindings: Declaration skillKey/file paths are concatenated into ordinary object keys; this service does not itself reject traversal, reserved keys or collisions.
Duplicate declaration keys are resolved by first match rather than rejected.
Binding upsert and import/adopt/bind are non-transactional read-then-write flows with no concurrency lock or idempotency key.
Reconcile automatically adopts any same-company canonical-key Skill without validating provenance or requiring an ownership-transfer decision.
Import uses onConflict:replace before binding; failure can overwrite or orphan resources without an atomic rollback receipt.
Every file-read error is swallowed as null drift, conflating storage/authorization/integrity outages with operator modifications.
Reset is destructive and unauthenticated at this service boundary; no human approval, pre-state digest or downstream assignment impact is recorded.
No package signature/license/hash, executable/data/egress admission, uninstall/upgrade/rollback or durable event/outbox handling exists.
